issue.title: TSAN failure with free-threaded build, test_daemon_threads_fatal_error

issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

It seems this unit test started failing after GH-140111.  Build with the following configure options: `./configure --with-thread-sanitizer --with-pydebug --disable-gil`.

Command to trigger the failure (doesn't happen every run).  
```
./python -m test test_threading -m test_daemon_threads_fatal_error
```

comments.body:
The issue is in the test itself, the tests runs a daemon thread with `sleep()` which releases the GIL however it is possible that by the time that runs the interpreter state is already freed so tsan reports it as data race with `drop_gil` and `free_interpreter`.

Currently the test works because the interpreter state is leaked, but that needs to be fixed. Also the test was recently changed in https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/a64881363b836b95fb4512a5689d69c1aa07ecb8 and previously a crash was expected.

I think this needs a similar fix as https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/130649 which is to add reference counting to interpreter states so that the interpreter state cannot be free prematurely before daemon threads are hung.

cc @colesbury
@kumaraditya303 So, there's no need to look for ways to fix this data race, and my (our) fix is correct?
Yes, our fix was correct but it exposed another race at shutdown which needs to fixed first

I have prepared a PR with a fix for this issue and with the previous leak fix.

CC: @kumaraditya303

> I think this needs a similar fix as https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/130649 which is to add reference counting to interpreter states so that the interpreter state cannot be free prematurely before daemon threads are hung.

I don't think this is an actual bug in practice. A thread doesn't need the interpreter to be valid in order to hang; all it needs is to read a single field on the thread state, which is atomically set by a finalizing interpreter (see [`_PyThreadState_MustExit`](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/9a87ce8b57f5d698900d84b4f6f5aa47b5f37a89/Python/pystate.c#L3009)). Because of Sam's patch that you linked, a thread could try to reacquire the GIL long after the interpreter has been deallocated, but it will still correctly hang.

In the `drop_gil` case that TSan is complaining about, I'm mostly sure it's a false positive, because the interpreter shouldn't be able to finalize in another thread when it doesn't hold the GIL.

As far as I can tell, the only way to actually trigger this is to create a thread state for an interpreter that is already finalizing and has already marked all other threads as "shutting down", but at that point, you're compromising thread-safety anyway, because we assume that there's only one thread left after calling `_PyThreadState_DeleteList`. 

Unless I missed a case where we call `_PyThreadState_MustExit` in an unsafe manner, I'm not convinced we should make finalization even more complicated to somewhat support something that people shouldn't do anyway. Play stupid games with finalization, win stupid crashes!

The race is real, not a false positive. The issue is in the very first line of `drop_gil()`:
```c
struct _ceval_state *ceval = &interp->ceval;
```
The daemon thread reads `interp->ceval` while the main thread is freeing the interpreter memory via `free_interpreter() `→ `PyMem_RawFree()` → `memset()`.

Timeline:
1. Main thread: `PyInterpreterState_Delete()` → `free_interpreter()` starts
2. Daemon thread: wakes from `time.sleep()` → `drop_gil()` → reads `interp->ceval`
3. Race: daemon reads from memory being freed by main thread

The `_PyThreadState_MustExit` check you mentioned happens in thread state, but `drop_gil()` accesses interpreter state first. The refcount ensures `PyInterpreterState` stays alive until all thread states (including daemons) are freed.

> Daemon thread: wakes from time.sleep() → drop_gil() → reads interp->ceval

Again, that shouldn't be possible. The daemon thread releases the GIL *before* it calls `sleep`, so when it wakes from `time.sleep`, it should be calling `take_gil`, not `drop_gil`. `take_gil` will correctly see that `_PyThreadState_MustExit` is set and hang before accessing the interpreter state.
@ZeroIntensity Got it—so we keep the leak-related fixes and remove the rest? Or will you just revert the previous revert and close this PR?)
I think we can just reapply #140111 and then add a suppression, but let's wait to hear from others first.

> Again, that shouldn't be possible. The daemon thread releases the GIL before it calls sleep, so when it wakes from time.sleep, it should be calling take_gil, not drop_gil. take_gil will correctly see that _PyThreadState_MustExit is set and hang before accessing the interpreter state.

You are correct but here the race happens while releasing the gil, the hanging of thread happens when it tries to acquire gil not when releasing the gil which can read freed memory while accessing interp state. 

Sequence:
- subinterpreters finalization starts
- daemon thread is executing and about to release gil for calling sleep
- finalization frees interp state of subinterpreter
- while releasing gil sub interpreter tries to access already freed memory

FWIW currently as a result of this bug all interpreter states created by modules like concurrent.interpreters would leak a significant amount of memory `sizeof(PyInterpreterState)=225568 bytes`.

cc @hugovk I think this should be a release blocker

> daemon thread is executing and about to release gil for calling sleep
> finalization frees interp state of subinterpreter

Finalization needs to hold the GIL or make a stop-the-world pause, which will wait until the daemon thread has released the GIL. It's impossible for the daemon thread to have the GIL and have its interpreter deallocate concurrently.

> Finalization needs to hold the GIL or make a stop-the-world pause, 

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/fbf0843e39e01ec8a8295f6475065b08053f13dd/Python/pylifecycle.c#L2110-L2120

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/fbf0843e39e01ec8a8295f6475065b08053f13dd/Python/pylifecycle.c#L2601-L2662

As per the comments, I don't see any stop the world pauses here, is it somewhere else?

I chatted with @ZeroIntensity and we both agreed to add a suppression for now and address the memory leak first, daemon threads is a new feature in subinterpreters and we can address more of that later.
